summary: Eberhard Sandschneider studied at Saarland University (~1976–1986, PhD). Working in sinology and other fields, he held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), the Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

A scholar of linguistics and other fields, Eberhard Schrader studied at the University of Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1854–1858). He held posts at Zurich (~1862–1870), Giessen (~1870–1873), Jena (~1873–1875), and the University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

Working in Indology and philosophy, Edeltraud Harzer studied at the University of Prague, the University of Washington (PhD), and under traditional teachers Shrinarayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Indiana, and UT Austin (1998).

Edgar H. Sturtevant, a linguist, studied at Illinois College (1893–1895) and Indiana University (~1895–1898). He subsequently held academic posts at Columbia University (~1908–1920) and Yale University (~1923–1943).

Edgar Thurston, who worked in history, archaeology, and other fields, was educated at Eton College and King's College London. He served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1885–1908).

Edith Wyschogrod worked in philosophy and religious studies after earning degrees at Hunter College (~1947–1951) and Columbia University (~1964–1970). She served as the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (1992–2002).
Edmond Yee works in religious studies and sinology. His career includes attested faculty appointments at both Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union in 2003.

Edmund Hardy studied at Mainz, Heidelberg (PhD under Kuno Fischer), Berlin, and Freiburg. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he held professorships at Freiburg (1885–1893), Fribourg (1894–1898), and Würzburg (~1893–1904).

Philosopher Edmund Husserl studied under Wilhelm Wundt and attended Leipzig, Berlin, Vienna, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1887–1901), the University of Göttingen (1901–1916), and the University of Freiburg (1916–1928).

Edmund Leach studied at Clare College, Cambridge, and the London School of Economics (PhD). Working in religious studies and other fields, he held posts at the LSE (~1947–1953), Cambridge (1953–1978; Provost of King's 1966–1979), and the RAI (1971–1975).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist who graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886. He also pursued studies under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Böhmer, a scholar in linguistics, studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1847–1850). He later held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872–1879).

Sinologist Eduard Erkes studied at the University of Leipzig (~1909–1913) under doctoral supervisor August Conrady. He later held posts at the University of Berlin and the University of Leipzig (~1917–1958).

Eduard Hermann studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena (PhD under Berthold Delbrück). Active in linguistics and Indology, he held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and the University of Göttingen (1917–1937).

Eduard Müller, who worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, completed his inaugural dissertation at the University of Leipzig (~1873–1874). He subsequently served as a professor at the University of Bern (~1887–1908).

Eduard Röer studied under J. F. Herbart and Franz Bopp at Königsberg and Jena. Working in Indology and philosophy, he held posts at Berlin (1833), the East India Company (~1839–1858), The Asiatic Society (1841, 1847), and Bibliotheca Indica (1847).

Eduard Sachau studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Fleischer, Brockhaus, and Nöldeke. Working in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and archaeology, he held posts at Vienna (1869), Berlin (1876), and the Seminar for Oriental Languages (1887).

Eduard Schwyzer was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1912–1927), the University of Bonn (~1927–1932), and the University of Berlin (~1932–1943).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach works in the field of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong, where he studied under supervisors Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias (attested 2014).
